title: Implement Handles demand exchange and rewarded insight marketplace
description: Build a future Handles feature where Wheelwright users can express desired features, behavior requests, and telemetry-sharing preferences through an enrollment and bidding system. The system should support privacy-aware demand signals, optional rewarded participation, vendor-funded custom segment requests, and user benefit that stays inside the Wheelwright ecosystem as credit toward fresher data, premium insight access, and product influence. This should also support behavioral/taste data exchange, where users contribute usage signals in return for newer data, credits, or ranking access in a model similar to reward ecosystems such as Bing Rewards.
non_goals: Do not move private money directly between users and vendors in v1
Do not require sensitive raw tracks to be sold or exposed
Do not make local Wheelwright usefulness depend on marketplace participation
Do not include protected track-restoration plugins in this batch

must_be_sequential: 1. Define feature-demand enrollment and voting/request model.
2. Define Wheelwright credit economy where user participation earns spendable value inside Handles rather than external payout in v1.
3. Define vendor custom-segment request contract and how Wheelwright mediates access to insight rather than raw private data.
4. Define privacy, consent, trust, and anti-displacement rules so the operator relationship remains central.
5. Define how marketplace demand feeds roadmap and monetization without compromising core product trust.

verification_requirements: Verify the model uses privacy-aware demand and behavior insight rather than unrestricted raw-data selling
Verify user-earned value is spendable inside Handles as credits
Verify vendor requests are mediated through Wheelwright and cannot trivially displace the operator relationship
Verify this is framed as a future product layer, not a dependency for core routing or orchestration

acceptance_tests.expected: User value is captured as internal credits/benefits rather than uncontrolled cash movement in v1
Privacy, consent, and anti-displacement rules are first-class
Vendors can fund custom segments and insight access without requiring raw private track exposure

review_questions: Is the demand exchange economically coherent without forcing external cash rails in v1?
Are privacy and consent constraints strong enough to keep trust high?
Does the design preserve Wheelwright as the trusted intermediary rather than making it easy to displace?
implementer_review.block_reason: Cluster 1 hub infrastructure (routing table + Octo) must be operational before product/commercial layer can be implemented. website/ directory does not yet exist.

workflow.handoff_reason: Blocked until Cluster 1 ships. Do not claim.

marketplace_model.exchange_principle: Users may trade behavioral/taste data for value inside the Wheelwright ecosystem rather than only paying cash.
marketplace_model.vendor_value: Vendors and publishers can fund custom segment insight while Wheelwright mediates access and preserves trust.

notes: Expanded to include behavioral/taste data exchange, rankings, and rewards-style credit model.
blocking_conditions: implementation-hub-model-routing-table-v1 must be accepted (hub owns model routing)
implementation-octo-gardener-dispatch-v1 must be accepted (hub orchestration must exist)
website/ directory and hosting infrastructure must be established before implementation begins
